nodes.name: Tensor power and the sample moment tensor deviation
nodes.statement: For an integer \(p\ge2\), we study, in the sub-Gaussian and Gaussian settings, the deviation \[ \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} - \mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}, \] where \(X^{\otimes p}:=X\otimes\cdots\otimes X\) denotes the \(p\)-fold tensor product of \(X\), and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf F}\) denotes the Frobenius norm.
nodes.statement_short: Introduces the p-fold tensor power $X^{\otimes p}$ and the Frobenius deviation of the empirical moment tensor studied in the paper.

nodes.name: Asymptotic inequality notation
nodes.statement: We write \(a\lesssim_p b\) if \(a\le C_p b\) for a constant \(C_p>0\) that depends only on \(p\), and write \(a\asymp_p b\) if both \(a\lesssim_p b\) and \(b\lesssim_p a\). We omit the subscript when the implicit constants are universal.

nodes.name: Max and min notation
nodes.statement: We also write \(a\lor b:=\max\{a,b\}\) and \(a\land b:=\min\{a,b\}\).

nodes.name: Euclidean norm
nodes.statement: For a vector \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), we denote its Euclidean norm by \(\|x\|_2\).

nodes.name: Frobenius inner product and norm of tensors
nodes.statement: For order-\(p\) tensors \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_p}\), we define the Frobenius inner product and norm by $\langle A,B\rangle_{\mathsf F} := \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_p} A_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}B_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}$ and $ \|A\|_{\mathsf F} := \langle A,A\rangle_{\mathsf F}^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Operator norm of a tensor
nodes.statement: The operator norm of \(A\) is defined by $\|A\| := \sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_p\|_2\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|$.
nodes.statement_short: The operator norm of a tensor is the supremum of its pairing with rank-one tensors of unit vectors.

nodes.name: Orlicz psi_2 norm and L_q norm
nodes.statement: The Orlicz \(\psi_2\) norm and the \(L_q\) norm of a real-valued random variable \(Z\) are defined by \[ \|Z\|_{\psi_2} := \inf\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\{ t>0:\mathbb{E}\exp(Z^2/t^2)\le 2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\}, \qquad \|Z\|_{L_q} := \big(\mathbb{E}|Z|^q\big)^{1/q}. \]

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian random vector
nodes.statement: We say that a random vector \(X \in \mathbb{R}^d\) is sub-Gaussian if there exists \(K>0\) such that \begin{align} \|\langle X,v\rangle\|_{\psi_2} \le K \|\langle X,v\rangle\|_{L_2}, \qquad \text{for any } v\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}, \end{align} where $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ denotes the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d.$
nodes.statement_short: X is sub-Gaussian if every one-dimensional marginal has psi_2 norm at most K times its L_2 norm.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian condition (2.1)
nodes.statement: \|\langle X,v\rangle\|_{\psi_2} \le K \|\langle X,v\rangle\|_{L_2}, \qquad \text{for any } v\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1},
nodes.label: eq:def-subg

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian constant
nodes.statement: The smallest such constant $K>0$ is called the sub-Gaussian constant of $X$.

nodes.name: Gaussian distribution notation
nodes.statement: We use $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)$ to denote the Gaussian distribution with mean zero and covariance matrix $\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Nonzero covariance matrices
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, all covariance matrices are allowed to be singular, but are assumed to be nonzero.

nodes.name: Concentration of sample moment tensors
nodes.statement: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge 2\) be an integer. Then, for every \(q\ge1\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} - \mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right), \] where \[ \rho_p(\Sigma) := \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] Moreover, if $X$ is Gaussian, then \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \] where \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) := \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]
assumptions: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\).
conclusions: \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} - \mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup
\[ \rho_p(\Sigma) := \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]

\[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \]

\[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} - \mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup

\[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \]

nodes.statement_short: Sharp L_q bound on the Frobenius error of the empirical p-th moment tensor of a sub-Gaussian vector: trace, intermediate rho_p and large-deviation terms; two-sided for Gaussians.
nodes.label: thm:main1

nodes.name: Remarks on Theorem 2.1: sharpness, parity effect and tail bounds
nodes.statement: \leavevmode \begin{enumerate} \item The first upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} is sharp over the class of sub-Gaussian distributions. More precisely, in Example~\ref{example:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} we construct a centered random vector \(X\) with covariance \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\asymp1\) such that, for every integer \(p\ge2\), every \(q\ge1\), and i.i.d. copies \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) of \(X\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \] where \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\) is defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1}. Hence all three terms in the upper bound are necessary, up to constants depending only on \(p\). \item It is instructive to compare the sub-Gaussian and Gaussian bounds. The trace and large-deviation scales coincide in the two settings. When \(p\) is odd, the intermediate scales also coincide: \[ \rho_p(\Sigma) = \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}. \] By contrast, when \(p\) is even, \[ \rho_p(\Sigma)=\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, \qquad \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|. \] Thus, at even orders, passing from the Gaussian distribution to the full sub-Gaussian class may enlarge the covariance-dependent coefficient in the intermediate scale by the factor $ \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} /\|\Sigma\|, $ which can be as large as \(\sqrt{\operatorname{rank}(\Sigma)}\). This enlargement is intrinsic, as illustrated by Example~\ref{example:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness}; the parity effect is discussed further in Subsection \ref{subsec:sharpness}. \item Taking \(q=u\) in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} and applying Markov's inequality yields that, for every \(u\ge1\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{u\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{u^{p/2}}N \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \] If \(X\) is Gaussian, with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{u}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{u^{p/2}}{N}. \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The sub-Gaussian bound is sharp (Example 3.6); intermediate scales agree at odd p but can differ by sqrt(rank) at even p; Markov gives high-probability bounds.

nodes.name: Effective rank
nodes.statement: In operator norm, \cite[Theorems~4 and~9]{koltchinskii2017concentration} established sharp dimension-free bounds governed by the effective rank $r(\Sigma):=\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)/\|\Sigma\|$ using empirical-process methods.

nodes.name: Bunea-Xiao Frobenius-norm bound for the sample covariance
nodes.statement: Under a condition equivalent to \eqref{eq:def-subg}, Bunea and Xiao \cite[Proposition~A.3]{bunea2015sample} proved that, for \(u\ge1\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt{\frac{u}{N}} + \frac{u}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right), \qquad \widehat\Sigma_N := \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}X_i\otimes X_i. \]
nodes.statement_short: Under sub-Gaussianity, the sample covariance has Frobenius error at most Tr(Sigma)(sqrt(u/N)+u/N) with probability 1-e^{-u}.
conclusions: with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt{\frac{u}{N}} + \frac{u}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right), \qquad \widehat\Sigma_N := \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}X_i\otimes X_i. \]

nodes.name: Puchkin-Noskov-Spokoiny concentration of the squared Frobenius error
nodes.statement: Treating the regularity parameters in \cite[Assumption~2.1]{puchkin2025sharper} as fixed, their upper- and lower-tail bounds imply that, for every \(u\ge1\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2} - \mathbb{E}\|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| \lesssim \frac{ \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2}\sqrt{u} + \|\Sigma\|^{2}u }{N}, \] provided that $N \gtrsim r(\Sigma)^6+u^2r(\Sigma)^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Under their regularity assumption, the squared Frobenius error of the sample covariance concentrates at scale (||Sigma||_F^2 sqrt(u)+||Sigma||^2 u)/N when N is large.
assumptions: Treating the regularity parameters in \cite[Assumption~2.1]{puchkin2025sharper} as fixed
conclusions: with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2} - \mathbb{E}\|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| \lesssim \frac{ \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2}\sqrt{u} + \|\Sigma\|^{2}u }{N}, \]

nodes.name: High-probability Frobenius bound for the sample covariance (p=2)
nodes.statement: In particular, for every \(u\ge1\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)}{\sqrt N} + \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \sqrt{\frac{u\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|\frac{u}{N}. \]
nodes.statement_short: For p=2: with probability 1-e^{-u}, the sample covariance error is at most Tr/sqrt(N) + ||Sigma||_F sqrt((u^N)/N) + ||Sigma|| u/N.
conclusions: with probability at least \(1-e^{-u}\), \[ \|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \lesssim \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)}{\sqrt N} + \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \sqrt{\frac{u\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|\frac{u}{N}. \]

nodes.name: Proof idea of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} is given in Section~\ref{sec:proof1}. We briefly describe its main steps here to explain the role of the polynomial moment bound developed in the next subsection. For \(1\le i\le N\), set \(Z_i:=X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\). For \(q\ge2\), Lemma~\ref{lem:Hilbert-moment-reduction} gives \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp{}& \frac1N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} + \frac1N \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}}. \end{align*} This reduces the strong moments of the tensor-valued sum to a square-function moment and the weak moments of its scalar projections. The square-function term is controlled using moment bounds for \(\|X\|_2\) and Lata{\l}a's estimate for sums of nonnegative random variables \cite{latala1997estimation}. For the weak-moment term, Lata{\l}a's estimate for centered sums further reduces the problem to estimating the weak moments of a single centered tensor power: \begin{equation} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q},\qquad q\ge 1. \end{equation} Obtaining the required bound for a general sub-Gaussian vector \(X\) is the main challenge. This is precisely where Theorem~\ref{thm:main2}, the polynomial moment bound under Gaussian convex domination developed in the next subsection, enters the argument.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: Lemma 3.1 splits strong moments into a square function and weak moments; Latala's estimates reduce the latter to weak moments of one centered tensor power, supplied by Theorem 2.2.

nodes.name: Square-function and weak-moment reduction
nodes.statement: For \(1\le i\le N\), set \(Z_i:=X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\). For \(q\ge2\), Lemma~\ref{lem:Hilbert-moment-reduction} gives \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp{}& \frac1N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} + \frac1N \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}}. \end{align*} This reduces the strong moments of the tensor-valued sum to a square-function moment and the weak moments of its scalar projections.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.1 to the centered tensors Z_i.

nodes.name: Control of the square-function term
nodes.statement: The square-function term is controlled using moment bounds for \(\|X\|_2\) and Lata{\l}a's estimate for sums of nonnegative random variables \cite{latala1997estimation}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the square function via moments of ||X||_2 and Latala's estimate.

nodes.name: Reduction to a single centered tensor power
nodes.statement: For the weak-moment term, Lata{\l}a's estimate for centered sums further reduces the problem to estimating the weak moments of a single centered tensor power: \begin{equation} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q},\qquad q\ge 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Latala's centered-sum estimate reduces to the weak moment (2.2).

nodes.name: Weak-moment target (2.2)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q},\qquad q\ge 1.
nodes.label: eq:weak-moment-target

nodes.name: Role of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Obtaining the required bound for a general sub-Gaussian vector \(X\) is the main challenge. This is precisely where Theorem~\ref{thm:main2}, the polynomial moment bound under Gaussian convex domination developed in the next subsection, enters the argument.

nodes.name: Convex order
nodes.statement: Let \(U\) and \(V\) be random vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\). We say that \(U\) is dominated by \(V\) in convex order, and write \(U\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}V\), if $\mathbb{E}\varphi(U)\le\mathbb{E}\varphi(V)$ for every convex function \(\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\).

nodes.name: van Handel's Gaussian convex domination of sub-Gaussian vectors
nodes.statement: A recent result of van Handel \cite[Theorem~1.1]{vanhandel2025subgaussian} shows that sub-Gaussian random vectors are dominated in convex order by Gaussian random vectors. More precisely, in the setting of \eqref{eq:def-subg}, \begin{align} (CK)^{-1}X \preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} G_\Sigma, \end{align} where $C$ is a universal constant and \(G_\Sigma\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\).

nodes.name: Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination

Then, for every integer \(p\ge1\), every \(q\ge1\), every finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and every \(p\)-linear map \[ T:(\mathbb R^d)^p\to\mathcal H, \] one has \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \big\| T(Z,\ldots,Z) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \]

nodes.name: Derivation of the sub-Gaussian weak tensor moment estimate from Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: In particular, by \eqref{eq:convex-dominatation}, \(Z:=(CK)^{-1}X\) satisfies \(Z\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}G_\Sigma\) if $X$ is sub-Gaussian with sub-Gaussian constant $K$. Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} with \(\mathcal H=\mathbb R\) and \(T=T_A\) in \eqref{eq:T-A}, and using \(\|T_A\|_{\mathsf F}=\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\) together with \(\|V-\mathbb{E} V\|_{L_q}\le2\|V\|_{L_q}\), yields \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\lesssim_p K^p\Psi_p(q,\Sigma) \\ &\asymp_p K^p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, &p\text{ even},\\[4pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, &p\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align*} The final comparison follows because the terms defining \(\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) form a geometric progression.

nodes.name: Sharpness of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} is sharp for every \(\Sigma\succeq0\) and every \(q\ge1\). Indeed, since \(G_\Sigma\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}G_\Sigma\), the choice \(Z=G_\Sigma\) is admissible. Taking \(\mathcal H=\mathbb R\) and \(T=T_A\) as in \eqref{eq:T-A}, the noncentered Gaussian estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments} gives \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,G_\Sigma^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma). \] Thus, the martingale coupling argument used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main2}, outlined below and carried out in Section~\ref{sec:proof2}, recovers the sharp Gaussian scale under convex domination.

nodes.statement_short: Taking Z=G_Sigma and T=T_A, the Gaussian estimate of Lemma 3.5 shows Theorem 2.2 is sharp for every Sigma and q.

nodes.name: Proof idea of Theorem 2.2 (structured martingale coupling and conditional expansion)
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main2} is given in Section~\ref{sec:proof2}. Here we provide a high-level overview. Our starting point is a structural strengthening of Strassen's martingale coupling theorem obtained by Hua, Song, and Tudose in their recent resolution of Talagrand's convexity conjecture \cite{hua2026talagrand}. A classical theorem of Strassen \cite{strassen1965existence} gives an equivalent characterization of convex domination: \(U\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}V\) if and only if \(U\) and \(V\) admit a martingale coupling, that is, a coupling satisfying $\mathbb{E}[V\mid U]=U$. Strassen's theorem is an abstract existence result and gives no further information about the conditional laws of the coupling. In contrast, \cite[Proposition~3.3]{hua2026talagrand} states the following stronger structural result. Let \(U\) be a centered, finitely supported random vector, and let \(V\) be a centered random vector with an absolutely continuous law. If $U\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}(1-\varepsilon)V$ for some $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, then \(U\) and \(V\) admit a martingale coupling such that, for every \(u\in\mathrm{supp}(U)\), the conditional law of \(V\) given \(U=u\) has a log-concave density with respect to the law of \(V\). We apply this result in the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:main2}. A finite-support approximation and rescaling reduce the proof to the case of a finitely supported random vector \(Z\) satisfying \[ Z\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}(1-\varepsilon)G_\Sigma \qquad\text{for some }\varepsilon\in(0,1). \] Applying \cite[Proposition~3.3]{hua2026talagrand}, we obtain a martingale coupling of \(Z\) and \(G_\Sigma\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathrm{supp}(Z)\), the conditional law of \(G_\Sigma\) given \(Z=z\) has a log-concave density with respect to \(\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\). Set \(R:=G_\Sigma-Z\). For each integer \(r\ge1\), we define its conditional moment tensor by \[ M_r(Z):=\mathbb{E}[R^{\otimes r}\mid Z]. \] Since symmetrizing \(T\) does not change \(T(Z,\ldots,Z)\) and cannot increase \(\|T\|_{\mathsf F}\), we may assume without loss of generality that \(T\) is symmetric. For \(0\le r\le p\) and \(B\in(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}\), we write \[ T[Z^{p-r},B] := \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_r=1}^d B_{i_1,\ldots,i_r}\, T\bigl( \underbrace{Z,\ldots,Z}_{p-r\text{ times}}, e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_r} \bigr), \] where $(e_i)_{i=1}^d$ denote the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then, using multilinearity and symmetry of \(T\), and the fact that \(M_1(Z)=\mathbb{E}[R\mid Z]=0\), we obtain the expansion \begin{align} T[Z^p]=T(Z,\ldots,Z) = \underbrace{ \mathbb{E}\bigl[T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\mid Z\bigr] }_{\text{Gaussian contribution}} - \underbrace{ \sum_{r=2}^p \binom{p}{r} T[Z^{p-r},M_r(Z)] }_{\text{lower-degree contributions}}. \end{align} Thus the degree-\(p\) polynomial \(T(Z,\ldots,Z)\) is expressed as a conditional expectation of the corresponding Gaussian polynomial, minus correction terms of degree at most \(p-2\) in \(Z\), whose coefficients \(M_r(Z)\) are the conditional moment tensors of the remainder \(R\). This key identity is rigorously established in Equation \eqref{eq:Lq-conditional-expansion}.

nodes.name: Third moment tensor of isotropic log-concave vectors
nodes.statement: In a very recent work, Chen and Klartag determine the optimal universal constant in the thin-shell inequality \cite{chen2026thinshell}. Their Theorem 1.2 shows that every isotropic log-concave random vector \(Y\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfies the sharp estimate \[ \bigl\|\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes 3}\bigr\|_{\mathsf F}^{2} \le 4d. \] Equality is attained when the coordinates of $Y$ are independent standard, centered, exponential random variables. Thus, at order \(p=3\), a sharp estimate is available under mere log-concavity in the isotropic setting. By contrast, under the stronger assumption of uniform log-concavity, Proposition~\ref{prop:ULC-moment-tensors} provides anisotropic bounds at all orders needed for the structured martingale coupling argument in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main2}. It would be interesting to investigate sharp dimension-free, covariance-dependent Frobenius-norm bounds for higher-order moment tensors under mere log-concavity.

nodes.statement_short: Chen-Klartag give the sharp bound ||E Y^{otimes 3}||_F^2 <= 4d under mere log-concavity; Proposition 2.4 instead covers all orders under uniform log-concavity.
nodes.label: rem:ULC-third-moment

nodes.name: Proof idea of Theorem 2.2 (induction on the degree)
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement_short: Induction on p: the Gaussian term is bounded by Jensen and Proposition 2.3; each correction is bounded by Proposition 2.4 times the induction hypothesis for S_rT.

nodes.name: Base case p=1
nodes.statement: We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} by induction on the order \(p\). For \(p=1\) the map \(z\mapsto\|T(z)\|_{\mathcal H}^q\) is convex, so the estimate follows directly from convex domination and Proposition~\ref{prop:Hilbert-Gaussian-tensor-Lq}.
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement_short: Base case: convexity, convex domination and Proposition 2.3.

nodes.name: Gaussian contribution
nodes.statement: Let \(p\ge2\), and suppose the estimate holds at every degree \(\le p-1\). We start from the decomposition \eqref{eq:proof2-expansion}. By conditional Jensen's inequality and Proposition~\ref{prop:Hilbert-Gaussian-tensor-Lq}, the Gaussian contribution satisfies \begin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigl\| \mathbb{E}\bigl[T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\mid Z\bigr] \bigr\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigl\|T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\bigr\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step: bound the Gaussian term by conditional Jensen and Proposition 2.3.

nodes.name: Gaussian contribution bound (overview) (2.7)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigl\| \mathbb{E}\bigl[T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\mid Z\bigr] \bigr\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigl\|T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\bigr\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}.

nodes.name: Pointwise bound on corrections
nodes.statement: For the lower-degree contributions \(T[Z^{p-r},M_r(Z)]\), we define the \((p-r)\)-linear map \[ (\mathcal S_rT)(x_1,\ldots,x_{p-r}) := \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_r=1}^d T(x_1,\ldots,x_{p-r},e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_r}) \otimes e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_r}, \] with values in \(\mathcal H\otimes(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}\). Then $T[Z^{p-r},M_r(Z)] = \bigl\langle (\mathcal S_rT)(Z,\ldots,Z),\,M_r(Z) \bigr\rangle_{\mathsf F}$, where the pairing is taken over the last \(r\) tensor factors and leaves the \(\mathcal H\)-component untouched. Moreover \(\|\mathcal S_rT\|_{\mathsf F}=\|T\|_{\mathsf F}\), since \(\mathcal S_r\) only rearranges the coefficients of \(T\). By Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, \begin{align} \bigl\|T[Z^{p-r},M_r(Z)]\bigr\|_{\mathcal H} \le \|M_r(Z)\|_{\mathsf F}\, \bigl\|(\mathcal S_rT)(Z,\ldots,Z)\bigr\|_{\mathcal H\otimes(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement_short: Introduce S_rT and bound each correction by ||M_r||_F times ||S_rT(Z,...,Z)||.

nodes.name: Pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz bound (overview) (2.8)
nodes.statement: \bigl\|T[Z^{p-r},M_r(Z)]\bigr\|_{\mathcal H} \le \|M_r(Z)\|_{\mathsf F}\, \bigl\|(\mathcal S_rT)(Z,\ldots,Z)\bigr\|_{\mathcal H\otimes(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}}.
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.label: eq:proof2-pointwise

nodes.name: Uniform log-concavity of the remainder
nodes.statement: Conditionally on \(Z\), the law of \(R\) is a translate of the conditional law of \(G_\Sigma\) given \(Z\). Since the latter has a log-concave density with respect to \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\), the conditional law of \(R\) is \(\Sigma\)-uniformly log-concave. Therefore, Proposition~\ref{prop:ULC-moment-tensors} gives \(\|M_r(Z)\|_{\mathsf F}\lesssim_p\rho_r(\Sigma)\) almost surely.
nodes.section: 2.2 Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 2.4 bounds ||M_r(Z)||_F by rho_r(Sigma).

nodes.name: Close the induction
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:proof2-expansion}, \eqref{eq:proof2-Gaussian}, and \eqref{eq:proof2-low-degree} gives \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \big\| T(Z,\ldots,Z) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \] which proves the estimate at degree \(p\) and closes the induction. Note that the Hilbert-valued formulation of Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} is used in the induction: even for scalar-valued \(T\), the induction hypothesis is applied to the maps \(\mathcal S_rT\), which take values in \(\mathcal H\otimes(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}\).

nodes.name: Square-function and weak-moment reduction for Hilbert-valued sums
nodes.statement: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be independent centered random vectors in a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), let \(q\ge2\), and assume that \[ \|Z_i\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)} := \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} <\infty, \qquad i=1,\ldots,N. \] Then \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N Z_i \bigg\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)} \asymp \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} + \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}}. \]
assumptions: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be independent centered random vectors in a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\)
conclusions: Then \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N Z_i \bigg\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)} \asymp \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} + \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: For independent centered Hilbert-valued Z_i, ||sum Z_i||_{L_q} is equivalent, with universal constants, to the square-function moment plus the L_{q/2} weak moments.
nodes.label: lem:Hilbert-moment-reduction

nodes.name: Square-function estimate
nodes.statement: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge2\) be an integer. Then, for every \(q\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{equation} Moreover, if \(X\) is Gaussian, then \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \end{equation}
assumptions: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\).
conclusions: \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{equation}

then \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The square function (sum ||X_i^{otimes p}-E X^{otimes p}||_F^2)^{1/2} has L_q norm <~ K^p(sqrt(N)Tr^{p/2}+||Sigma||^{p/2}q^{p/2}), two-sided for Gaussians.
nodes.label: prop:master-common-diagonal

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian square-function bound (3.1)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right).

nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}.

nodes.name: Weak-moment estimate
nodes.statement: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge2\) be an integer. Then, for every \(q\ge1\), \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align} where \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\) is as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1}. Moreover, if \(X\) is Gaussian, then \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align} where \(\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\) is as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1}.
assumptions: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\).
conclusions: \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align}

then \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Weak moments sup_A ||sum <A, X_i^{otimes p}-E X^{otimes p}>||_{L_q} are bounded by rho_p(Sigma) sqrt(N(q^N)) (even p) or rho_p sqrt(Nq) (odd p) plus ||Sigma||^{p/2}q^{p/2}; Gaussian two-sided with rho_{p,G}.
nodes.label: prop:master-scalar-projections

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian weak-moment bound (3.3)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases}

nodes.name: Gaussian weak-moment two-sided bound (3.4)

nodes.label: eq:master-scalar-Gaussian

Consequently,  egin{align*} ho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{ rac qN} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2}\le  rac12 \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} +  rac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight). \end{align*} Thus the untruncated term is absorbed by the trace and large-deviation terms when \(q>N\). oindent	extbf{Gaussian case.} \medskip Combining \eqref{eq:master-apply-decoupling} with the Gaussian parts of Propositions~ef{prop:master-common-diagonal} and~ef{prop:master-scalar-projections} proves the asserted two-sided estimate directly when \(p\) is odd. When \(p\) is even, the same argument gives the asserted estimate together with the additional term $ho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q/N$. Since $ho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|$, we have  egin{align*}  rac{ho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q}{N} \le  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q}{N}\lesssim_p  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{N} +  rac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}\le  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} +  rac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*} Hence the additional term is absorbed, and  egin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E}  igg\|  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} -\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  igg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/q} \asymp_p  rac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + ho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{ rac qN} +  rac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*} This proves the claims for \(q\ge2\). Finally, let \(1\le q<2\). By monotonicity and the comparability of the corresponding rates at \(q\) and \(2\), the upper bounds follow from the case \(q=2\). In the Gaussian case, finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} gives \[ \mathbb{E} igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)  igg\|_{\mathsf F} \gtrsim_p \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E} igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)  igg\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2}. \] Monotonicity and rate comparability then extend the Gaussian lower bound from \(q=2\) to \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.1 to the centered tensors and combine with Propositions 3.2 and 3.3; absorb the extra odd/even terms into the trace and large-deviation scales, and extend to q<2 by monotonicity.

nodes.name: Reduction via Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: We first consider \(q\ge2\). Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:Hilbert-moment-reduction} in \((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\), equipped with the Frobenius inner product, to the independent centered tensors \[ X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,N, \] and then dividing the resulting equivalence by \(N\), we obtain \begin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} & \asymp \frac1N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}\nonumber\\ &\quad + \frac1N \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A, X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}. \end{align} In applying Proposition~\ref{prop:master-scalar-projections} below, replacing \(q/2\) by \(q\) on its right-hand side changes the estimates only by constants depending on \(p\).
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.1 to the centered tensors to get (3.5).

nodes.name: Reduction via Lemma 3.1 (3.5)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} & \asymp \frac1N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}\nonumber\\ &\quad + \frac1N \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\le1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A, X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}.
nodes.label: eq:master-apply-decoupling

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian case
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-Gaussian case.} \medskip Combining \eqref{eq:master-apply-decoupling} with the sub-Gaussian parts of Propositions~\ref{prop:master-common-diagonal} and~\ref{prop:master-scalar-projections} proves the asserted bound directly when \(p\) is even. When \(p\ge3\) is odd, the same estimates give the asserted bound except that $\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$ is replaced by $\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN}$. If \(q\le N\), these quantities coincide. If \(q>N\), then \[ \rho_p(\Sigma)^2 \le \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \qquad Nq\le\sqrt N\,q^{p/2}, \] where we used \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\|\Sigma\|\), \(\|\Sigma\|\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), and \(p\ge3\). Consequently, \begin{align*} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2}\le \frac12 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*} Thus the untruncated term is absorbed by the trace and large-deviation terms when \(q>N\). We therefore obtain \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} -\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine (3.5) with Propositions 3.2 and 3.3 in the sub-Gaussian case.

nodes.name: Combine the propositions
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:master-apply-decoupling} with the sub-Gaussian parts of Propositions~\ref{prop:master-common-diagonal} and~\ref{prop:master-scalar-projections} proves the asserted bound directly when \(p\) is even. When \(p\ge3\) is odd, the same estimates give the asserted bound except that $\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$ is replaced by $\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN}$.
nodes.statement_short: Even p follows directly; odd p gives an untruncated term.

nodes.name: Absorb the untruncated term
nodes.statement: If \(q\le N\), these quantities coincide. If \(q>N\), then \[ \rho_p(\Sigma)^2 \le \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \qquad Nq\le\sqrt N\,q^{p/2}, \] where we used \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\|\Sigma\|\), \(\|\Sigma\|\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), and \(p\ge3\). Consequently, \begin{align*} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2}\le \frac12 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For q>N the odd-order term is bounded by the geometric mean of the trace and large-deviation terms.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian bound
nodes.statement: Thus the untruncated term is absorbed by the trace and large-deviation terms when \(q>N\). We therefore obtain \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} -\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the sub-Gaussian upper bound.

nodes.name: Gaussian case
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian case.} \medskip Combining \eqref{eq:master-apply-decoupling} with the Gaussian parts of Propositions~\ref{prop:master-common-diagonal} and~\ref{prop:master-scalar-projections} proves the asserted two-sided estimate directly when \(p\) is odd. When \(p\) is even, the same argument gives the asserted estimate together with the additional term $\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q/N$. Since $\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q}{N} \le \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q}{N}\lesssim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}\le \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*} Hence the additional term is absorbed, and \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} -\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*} This proves the claims for \(q\ge2\).
nodes.statement_short: Combine (3.5) with the Gaussian parts of the propositions.

nodes.name: Combine the Gaussian estimates
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:master-apply-decoupling} with the Gaussian parts of Propositions~\ref{prop:master-common-diagonal} and~\ref{prop:master-scalar-projections} proves the asserted two-sided estimate directly when \(p\) is odd. When \(p\) is even, the same argument gives the asserted estimate together with the additional term $\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q/N$.
nodes.statement_short: Odd p is direct; even p leaves an extra term.

nodes.name: Bound the extra term
nodes.statement: Since $\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)q}{N} \le \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q}{N}\lesssim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}\le \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The extra even-order term is dominated by the trace and large-deviation terms.

nodes.name: Gaussian two-sided estimate
nodes.statement: Hence the additional term is absorbed, and \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p} -\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \asymp_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \frac{\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{align*} This proves the claims for \(q\ge2\).
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the two-sided Gaussian estimate.

nodes.name: The range 1<=q<2
nodes.statement: Finally, let \(1\le q<2\). By monotonicity and the comparability of the corresponding rates at \(q\) and \(2\), the upper bounds follow from the case \(q=2\). In the Gaussian case, finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} gives \[ \mathbb{E}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \gtrsim_p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2}. \] Monotonicity and rate comparability then extend the Gaussian lower bound from \(q=2\) to \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to q<2 by monotonicity and finite-chaos moment comparison.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement:
\medskip 
oindent	extbf{Sub-Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), set \[ W_i :=  ig\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \] Then, for \(q\ge2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  igg( \sum_{i=1}^N  ig\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2  igg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q} =  igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i  igg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2}. \] The positive semi-definite quadratic-form inequality \cite[Theorem~2.1 and Remark~2.2]{hsu2012tail}, see also \cite[Lemma~2.7 and Remark~2.8]{zhivotovskiy2024dimension}, implies that, for every \(t>0\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-t}\), \[ \|X\|_2 \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+t\|\Sigma\| }. \] Integrating this tail bound gives  egin{equation*} \|\|X\|_2\|_{L_s} \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+s\|\Sigma\| }, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation*} Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), the triangle inequality and Jensen's inequality give \[  ig\| X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  ig\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|X\|_2^p+\mathbb{E}\|X\|_2^p. \] Consequently, for every \(s\ge1\),  egin{align} \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  ig\| X_1^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  ig\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_{2s}}^2 \le 4\|\|X\|_2\|_{L_{2ps}}^{2p} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight). \end{align} Fix \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\). Applying Lata{\l}a's moment estimate for sums of i.i.d.\ nonnegative random variables \cite[Corollary~1]{latala1997estimation} with moment parameter \(r\), we obtain  egin{equation}  igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i  igg\|_{L_r} \asymp \sup_{\max\{1,r/N\}\le s\le r}  rac{r}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac Nr \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/s} \|W_1\|_{L_s}. \end{equation} Substituting \eqref{eq:Wi-moment-short} into \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, optimizing over \(s\), and using \(\|\Sigma\|\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), we obtain \[  igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i  igg\|_{L_r} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \Big( N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p + r^p\|\Sigma\|^p \Big). \] Since \(r=q/2\), it follows that  egin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  igg( \sum_{i=1}^N  ig\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}  ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2  igg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q}=  igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i  igg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight). \end{align*} For \(1\le q<2\), the same conclusion follows from the case \(q=2\) and monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms. This completes the proof of the upper bound for sub-Gaussian random vectors. \medskip 
oindent 	extbf{Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip When \(X\) is Gaussian, the upper bound follows immediately from the sub-Gaussian estimate above, since a centered Gaussian random vector satisfies \eqref{eq:def-subg} with \(K=\sqrt{8/3}\). \medskip 
oindent	extbf{Gaussian lower bound.} \medskip Suppose now that \(X=G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\). We first treat \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\ge1\). \medskip 	extbf{Step 1: a lower bound for \(\|W_1\|_{L_s}\).} We claim that  egin{equation} \|W_1\|_{L_s} \gtrsim_p \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation} Since \[ \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_{2s}}^2, \] it suffices to bound the latter norm below by \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\) and by \(s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\) separately. Let \(v_1\) be a unit top eigenvector of \(\Sigma\) and set \(\xi_1:=\|\Sigma\|^{-1/2}\langle G,v_1angle\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)\). Testing against \(A:=v_1^{\otimes p}\), which satisfies \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), gives \[  ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle A,G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight| = \|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight|. \] Since \(\|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\|_{L_{2s}}\asymp_p s^{p/2}\) for \(s\ge1\),  egin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_{2s}} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}s^{p/2}. \end{equation} For the trace scale, recall that by Wick's formula \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}=0\) when \(p\) is odd, while for \(p\) even \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\) is a sum of \((p-1)!!\) tensors, each obtained by permuting the legs of \(\Sigma^{\otimes p/2}\) and therefore of Frobenius norm \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}\). Hence, with \(b_p:=(p-1)!!\),  egin{equation}  ig\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \le b_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation} Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), orthogonality of the mean and the fluctuation in \((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\) together with Jensen's inequality gives  egin{align} \mathbb{E} ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^{2p} -  ig\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2
onumber\ &\ge \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(\mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^p - b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p-b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p. \end{align} By \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\|\Sigma\|\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), \[ b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p \le b_p^2 \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac{\|\Sigma\|}{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{p/2}. \] Set \(\kappa_p:=(2b_p^2)^{2/p}\). If \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\ge\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), the right-hand side is at most \(	frac12\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\), so \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-L2-identity} and \(2s\ge2\) yield  egin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_{2s}} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  ig\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_2} \ge 2^{-1/2}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}. \end{equation} If instead \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)<\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), then, since \(s\ge1\), \[ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \] so the trace scale is already controlled by \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale}. In either case, combining \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale} and \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-trace-scale} and squaring proves \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower}. \medskip 	extbf{Step 2: the two-sided Latała's estimate.} We use \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, which is an equivalence, and bound the supremum from below by evaluating it at two admissible values of \(s\). Take first \(s:=\max\{1,r/N\}\). If \(r\le N\), then \(s=1\) and the corresponding term equals \(N\|W_1\|_{L_1}\). If \(r>N\), then \(s=r/N\) and the corresponding term equals \[ N\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( rac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{N/r}\|W_1\|_{L_{r/N}} \ge e^{-1/e}N\|W_1\|_{L_1}, \] where we used \(\inf_{0<x\le1}x^x=e^{-1/e}\) and monotonicity of \(L_s\)-norms. In both cases, \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower} with \(s=1\) gives a lower bound \(\gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\). Taking instead \(s:=r\), and using \(N\ge1\) together with \(\max_{r\ge1}r^{-1}\log r=1/e\), we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( rac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/r}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \ge e^{-1/e}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p r^p\|\Sigma\|^p. \] Consequently, \[  igg\|\sum_{i=1}^N W_i igg\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+r^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \] and, taking square roots with \(r=q/2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  igg( \sum_{i=1}^N  ig\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2  igg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \] \medskip 	extbf{Step 3: the range \(1\le q<2\).} The upper bound follows from the case \(q=2\) by monotonicity. For the lower bound, note that \[ V:=  igg( \sum_{i=1}^N  ig\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} ig\|_{\mathsf F}^2  igg)^{1/2} =  ig\| \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)_{i=1}^N  ig\|_{\ell_2^N((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p})}, \] and that \(\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)_{i=1}^N\) is a Hilbert-space-valued Gaussian chaos of order at most \(p\) in the Gaussian vector \((G_1,\ldots,G_N)\).
