nodes.statement_short: Upper bound: moments of ||X||_2 and Latala's estimate for nonnegative sums. Lower bound: evaluate the two-sided Latala supremum at s=1 and s=r using Gaussian lower bounds for ||W_1||_{L_s}.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), set \[ W_i := \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \] Then, for \(q\ge2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} = \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2}. \] The positive semi-definite quadratic-form inequality \cite[Theorem~2.1 and Remark~2.2]{hsu2012tail}, see also \cite[Lemma~2.7 and Remark~2.8]{zhivotovskiy2024dimension}, implies that, for every \(t>0\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-t}\), \[ \|X\|_2 \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+t\|\Sigma\| }. \] Integrating this tail bound gives \begin{equation*} \|\|X\|_2\|_{L_s} \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+s\|\Sigma\| }, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation*} Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), the triangle inequality and Jensen's inequality give \[ \big\| X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|X\|_2^p+\mathbb{E}\|X\|_2^p. \] Consequently, for every \(s\ge1\), \begin{align} \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\| X_1^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2 \le 4\|\|X\|_2\|_{L_{2ps}}^{2p} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align} Fix \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\). Applying Lata{\l}a's moment estimate for sums of i.i.d.\ nonnegative random variables \cite[Corollary~1]{latala1997estimation} with moment parameter \(r\), we obtain \begin{equation} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_r} \asymp \sup_{\max\{1,r/N\}\le s\le r} \frac{r}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac Nr \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|W_1\|_{L_s}. \end{equation} Substituting \eqref{eq:Wi-moment-short} into \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, optimizing over \(s\), and using \(\|\Sigma\|\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), we obtain \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_r} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \Big( N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p + r^p\|\Sigma\|^p \Big). \] Since \(r=q/2\), it follows that \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}= \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*} For \(1\le q<2\), the same conclusion follows from the case \(q=2\) and monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms. This completes the proof of the upper bound for sub-Gaussian random vectors.
nodes.statement_short: Moments of ||X||_2 and Latala's estimate for nonnegative sums.

nodes.name: Define W_i
nodes.statement: For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), set \[ W_i := \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \] Then, for \(q\ge2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} = \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the square function via W_i.

nodes.name: Moments of the Euclidean norm
nodes.statement: The positive semi-definite quadratic-form inequality \cite[Theorem~2.1 and Remark~2.2]{hsu2012tail}, see also \cite[Lemma~2.7 and Remark~2.8]{zhivotovskiy2024dimension}, implies that, for every \(t>0\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-t}\), \[ \|X\|_2 \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+t\|\Sigma\| }. \] Integrating this tail bound gives \begin{equation*} \|\|X\|_2\|_{L_s} \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+s\|\Sigma\| }, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Hsu-Kakade-Zhang tail bound for ||X||_2, integrated.

nodes.name: Euclidean norm moment bound
nodes.statement: \|\|X\|_2\|_{L_s} \lesssim K \sqrt{ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)+s\|\Sigma\| }, \qquad s\ge1.
nodes.label: eq:subg-Euclidean-moment

nodes.name: Moments of W_1
nodes.statement: Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), the triangle inequality and Jensen's inequality give \[ \big\| X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|X\|_2^p+\mathbb{E}\|X\|_2^p. \] Consequently, for every \(s\ge1\), \begin{align} \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\| X_1^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2 \le 4\|\|X\|_2\|_{L_{2ps}}^{2p} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound ||W_1||_{L_s} by moments of ||X||_2.

nodes.name: Moment bound for W_1 (3.6)
nodes.statement: \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\| X_1^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2 \le 4\|\|X\|_2\|_{L_{2ps}}^{2p} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right).
nodes.label: eq:Wi-moment-short

nodes.name: Latala estimate for nonnegative sums
nodes.statement: Fix \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\). Applying Lata{\l}a's moment estimate for sums of i.i.d.\ nonnegative random variables \cite[Corollary~1]{latala1997estimation} with moment parameter \(r\), we obtain \begin{equation} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_r} \asymp \sup_{\max\{1,r/N\}\le s\le r} \frac{r}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac Nr \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|W_1\|_{L_s}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Latala's estimate for i.i.d. nonnegative sums.

nodes.name: Latala estimate for the square function (3.7)
nodes.statement: \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_r} \asymp \sup_{\max\{1,r/N\}\le s\le r} \frac{r}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac Nr \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|W_1\|_{L_s}.
nodes.label: eq:Latala-square-function

nodes.name: Optimize over s
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{eq:Wi-moment-short} into \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, optimizing over \(s\), and using \(\|\Sigma\|\le\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), we obtain \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_r} \lesssim_p K^{2p} \Big( N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p + r^p\|\Sigma\|^p \Big). \] Since \(r=q/2\), it follows that \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\| X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}= \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N W_i \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}}^{1/2} \lesssim_p K^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute and optimize over s.

nodes.name: Range q<2
nodes.statement: For \(1\le q<2\), the same conclusion follows from the case \(q=2\) and monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms. This completes the proof of the upper bound for sub-Gaussian random vectors.
nodes.statement_short: Extend by monotonicity of L_q norms.

nodes.name: Gaussian upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip When \(X\) is Gaussian, the upper bound follows immediately from the sub-Gaussian estimate above, since a centered Gaussian random vector satisfies \eqref{eq:def-subg} with \(K=\sqrt{8/3}\).
nodes.statement_short: Gaussians are sub-Gaussian with K=sqrt(8/3).

nodes.name: Gaussian lower bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian lower bound.} \medskip Suppose now that \(X=G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\). We first treat \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\ge1\). \medskip \textbf{Step 1: a lower bound for \(\|W_1\|_{L_s}\).} We claim that \begin{equation} \|W_1\|_{L_s} \gtrsim_p \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation} Since \[ \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2, \] it suffices to bound the latter norm below by \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\) and by \(s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\) separately. Let \(v_1\) be a unit top eigenvector of \(\Sigma\) and set \(\xi_1:=\|\Sigma\|^{-1/2}\langle G,v_1\rangle\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)\). Testing against \(A:=v_1^{\otimes p}\), which satisfies \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), gives \[ \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| = \|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|. \] Since \(\|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\|_{L_{2s}}\asymp_p s^{p/2}\) for \(s\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}s^{p/2}. \end{equation} For the trace scale, recall that by Wick's formula \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}=0\) when \(p\) is odd, while for \(p\) even \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\) is a sum of \((p-1)!!\) tensors, each obtained by permuting the legs of \(\Sigma^{\otimes p/2}\) and therefore of Frobenius norm \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}\). Hence, with \(b_p:=(p-1)!!\), \begin{equation} \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \le b_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation} Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), orthogonality of the mean and the fluctuation in \((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\) together with Jensen's inequality gives \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^{2p} - \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2\nonumber\\ &\ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^p - b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p-b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p. \end{align} By \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\|\Sigma\|\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), \[ b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p \le b_p^2 \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\|\Sigma\|}{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{p/2}. \] Set \(\kappa_p:=(2b_p^2)^{2/p}\). If \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\ge\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), the right-hand side is at most \(\tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\), so \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-L2-identity} and \(2s\ge2\) yield \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2} \ge 2^{-1/2}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}. \end{equation} If instead \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)<\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), then, since \(s\ge1\), \[ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \] so the trace scale is already controlled by \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale}. In either case, combining \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale} and \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-trace-scale} and squaring proves \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower}. \medskip \textbf{Step 2: the two-sided Latała's estimate.} We use \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, which is an equivalence, and bound the supremum from below by evaluating it at two admissible values of \(s\). Take first \(s:=\max\{1,r/N\}\). If \(r\le N\), then \(s=1\) and the corresponding term equals \(N\|W_1\|_{L_1}\). If \(r>N\), then \(s=r/N\) and the corresponding term equals \[ N\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{N/r}\|W_1\|_{L_{r/N}} \ge e^{-1/e}N\|W_1\|_{L_1}, \] where we used \(\inf_{0<x\le1}x^x=e^{-1/e}\) and monotonicity of \(L_s\)-norms. In both cases, \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower} with \(s=1\) gives a lower bound \(\gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\). Taking instead \(s:=r\), and using \(N\ge1\) together with \(\max_{r\ge1}r^{-1}\log r=1/e\), we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/r}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \ge e^{-1/e}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p r^p\|\Sigma\|^p. \] Consequently, \[ \bigg\|\sum_{i=1}^N W_i\bigg\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+r^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \] and, taking square roots with \(r=q/2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \] \medskip \textbf{Step 3: the range \(1\le q<2\).} The upper bound follows from the case \(q=2\) by monotonicity. For the lower bound, note that \[ V:= \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} = \big\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i=1}^N \big\|_{\ell_2^N((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p})}, \] and that \(\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i=1}^N\) is a Hilbert-space-valued Gaussian chaos of order at most \(p\) in the Gaussian vector \((G_1,\ldots,G_N)\). Finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} therefore gives \[ \|V\|_{L_2} \lesssim_p \|V\|_{L_1} \le \|V\|_{L_q}. \] Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:master-diagonal-g} at \(q=2\) is comparable, up to constants depending only on \(p\), to its value at \(q\in[1,2)\), the lower bound extends to \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound via the two-sided Latala estimate.

nodes.name: Gaussian setting
nodes.statement: Suppose now that \(X=G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\). We first treat \(q\ge2\) and set \(r:=q/2\ge1\).
nodes.statement_short: Set X=G Gaussian and r=q/2.

nodes.name: Step 1: lower bound for ||W_1||_{L_s}
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 1: a lower bound for \(\|W_1\|_{L_s}\).} We claim that \begin{equation} \|W_1\|_{L_s} \gtrsim_p \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation} Since \[ \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2, \] it suffices to bound the latter norm below by \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\) and by \(s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\) separately. Let \(v_1\) be a unit top eigenvector of \(\Sigma\) and set \(\xi_1:=\|\Sigma\|^{-1/2}\langle G,v_1\rangle\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)\). Testing against \(A:=v_1^{\otimes p}\), which satisfies \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), gives \[ \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| = \|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|. \] Since \(\|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\|_{L_{2s}}\asymp_p s^{p/2}\) for \(s\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}s^{p/2}. \end{equation} For the trace scale, recall that by Wick's formula \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}=0\) when \(p\) is odd, while for \(p\) even \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\) is a sum of \((p-1)!!\) tensors, each obtained by permuting the legs of \(\Sigma^{\otimes p/2}\) and therefore of Frobenius norm \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}\). Hence, with \(b_p:=(p-1)!!\), \begin{equation} \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \le b_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation} Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), orthogonality of the mean and the fluctuation in \((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\) together with Jensen's inequality gives \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^{2p} - \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2\nonumber\\ &\ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^p - b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p-b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p. \end{align} By \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\|\Sigma\|\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), \[ b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p \le b_p^2 \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\|\Sigma\|}{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{p/2}. \] Set \(\kappa_p:=(2b_p^2)^{2/p}\). If \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\ge\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), the right-hand side is at most \(\tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\), so \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-L2-identity} and \(2s\ge2\) yield \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2} \ge 2^{-1/2}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}. \end{equation} If instead \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)<\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), then, since \(s\ge1\), \[ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \] so the trace scale is already controlled by \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale}. In either case, combining \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale} and \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-trace-scale} and squaring proves \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower}.
nodes.statement_short: Show ||W_1||_{L_s} >~ Tr^p + s^p||Sigma||^p.

nodes.name: Claim and reduction
nodes.statement: We claim that \begin{equation} \|W_1\|_{L_s} \gtrsim_p \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \qquad s\ge1. \end{equation} Since \[ \|W_1\|_{L_s} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}}^2, \] it suffices to bound the latter norm below by \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}\) and by \(s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\) separately.
nodes.statement_short: State the claim and reduce to two separate lower bounds.

nodes.name: Gaussian lower bound for ||W_1||_{L_s} (3.8)
nodes.statement: \|W_1\|_{L_s} \gtrsim_p \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+s^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \qquad s\ge1.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-W1-lower

nodes.name: Tail scale
nodes.statement: Let \(v_1\) be a unit top eigenvector of \(\Sigma\) and set \(\xi_1:=\|\Sigma\|^{-1/2}\langle G,v_1\rangle\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)\). Testing against \(A:=v_1^{\otimes p}\), which satisfies \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), gives \[ \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| = \|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|. \] Since \(\|\xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p\|_{L_{2s}}\asymp_p s^{p/2}\) for \(s\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}s^{p/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Test against v_1^{otimes p} to get the s^{p/2}||Sigma||^{p/2} scale.

nodes.name: Tail-scale lower bound (3.9)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}s^{p/2}.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale

nodes.name: Mean tensor bound via Wick's formula
nodes.statement: For the trace scale, recall that by Wick's formula \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}=0\) when \(p\) is odd, while for \(p\) even \(\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\) is a sum of \((p-1)!!\) tensors, each obtained by permuting the legs of \(\Sigma^{\otimes p/2}\) and therefore of Frobenius norm \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}\). Hence, with \(b_p:=(p-1)!!\), \begin{equation} \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \le b_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Wick's formula bounds ||E G^{otimes p}||_F.

nodes.name: Gaussian mean tensor bound (3.10)
nodes.statement: \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \le b_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-mean-tensor-upper

nodes.name: Second-moment lower bound
nodes.statement: Since \(\|x^{\otimes p}\|_{\mathsf F}=\|x\|_2^p\), orthogonality of the mean and the fluctuation in \((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\) together with Jensen's inequality gives \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^{2p} - \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2\nonumber\\ &\ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^p - b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p-b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p. \end{align} By \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2\le\|\Sigma\|\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\), \[ b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p \le b_p^2 \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac{\|\Sigma\|}{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{p/2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality and Jensen give Tr^p - b_p^2||Sigma||_F^p.

nodes.name: Second-moment identity for centered Gaussian tensor power (3.11)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^{2p} - \big\|\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2\nonumber\\ &\ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|G\|_2^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^p - b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p-b_p^2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^p.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-W1-L2-identity

nodes.name: Case Tr large
nodes.statement: Set \(\kappa_p:=(2b_p^2)^{2/p}\). If \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\ge\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), the right-hand side is at most \(\tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\), so \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-L2-identity} and \(2s\ge2\) yield \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2} \ge 2^{-1/2}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If Tr(Sigma) >= kappa_p||Sigma||, the L_2 norm already gives the trace scale.

nodes.name: Trace-scale lower bound (3.12)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{2s}} \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \big\|G^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2} \ge 2^{-1/2}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-W1-trace-scale

nodes.name: Case Tr small
nodes.statement: If instead \(\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)<\kappa_p\|\Sigma\|\), then, since \(s\ge1\), \[ \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \le \kappa_p^{p/2}s^{p/2}\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}, \] so the trace scale is already controlled by \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale}.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise the trace scale is dominated by the tail scale.

nodes.name: Conclude Step 1
nodes.statement: In either case, combining \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-tail-scale} and \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-trace-scale} and squaring proves \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine both scales.

nodes.name: Step 2: two-sided Latala estimate
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 2: the two-sided Latała's estimate.} We use \eqref{eq:Latala-square-function}, which is an equivalence, and bound the supremum from below by evaluating it at two admissible values of \(s\). Take first \(s:=\max\{1,r/N\}\). If \(r\le N\), then \(s=1\) and the corresponding term equals \(N\|W_1\|_{L_1}\). If \(r>N\), then \(s=r/N\) and the corresponding term equals \[ N\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{N/r}\|W_1\|_{L_{r/N}} \ge e^{-1/e}N\|W_1\|_{L_1}, \] where we used \(\inf_{0<x\le1}x^x=e^{-1/e}\) and monotonicity of \(L_s\)-norms. In both cases, \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower} with \(s=1\) gives a lower bound \(\gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\). Taking instead \(s:=r\), and using \(N\ge1\) together with \(\max_{r\ge1}r^{-1}\log r=1/e\), we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/r}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \ge e^{-1/e}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p r^p\|\Sigma\|^p. \] Consequently, \[ \bigg\|\sum_{i=1}^N W_i\bigg\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+r^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \] and, taking square roots with \(r=q/2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the Latala supremum at s=max(1,r/N) and s=r.

nodes.name: Evaluate at s=max(1,r/N)
nodes.statement: Take first \(s:=\max\{1,r/N\}\). If \(r\le N\), then \(s=1\) and the corresponding term equals \(N\|W_1\|_{L_1}\). If \(r>N\), then \(s=r/N\) and the corresponding term equals \[ N\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{N/r}\|W_1\|_{L_{r/N}} \ge e^{-1/e}N\|W_1\|_{L_1}, \] where we used \(\inf_{0<x\le1}x^x=e^{-1/e}\) and monotonicity of \(L_s\)-norms. In both cases, \eqref{eq:gaussian-W1-lower} with \(s=1\) gives a lower bound \(\gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p\).
nodes.statement_short: Gives the N Tr^p lower bound.

nodes.name: Evaluate at s=r
nodes.statement: Taking instead \(s:=r\), and using \(N\ge1\) together with \(\max_{r\ge1}r^{-1}\log r=1/e\), we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nr\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/r}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \ge e^{-1/e}\|W_1\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p r^p\|\Sigma\|^p. \] Consequently, \[ \bigg\|\sum_{i=1}^N W_i\bigg\|_{L_r} \gtrsim_p N\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^p+r^p\|\Sigma\|^p, \] and, taking square roots with \(r=q/2\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \sqrt N\,\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Gives the r^p||Sigma||^p lower bound; take square roots.

nodes.name: Step 3: the range 1<=q<2
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 3: the range \(1\le q<2\).} The upper bound follows from the case \(q=2\) by monotonicity. For the lower bound, note that \[ V:= \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \big\|G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\big\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} = \big\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i=1}^N \big\|_{\ell_2^N((\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p})}, \] and that \(\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i=1}^N\) is a Hilbert-space-valued Gaussian chaos of order at most \(p\) in the Gaussian vector \((G_1,\ldots,G_N)\). Finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} therefore gives \[ \|V\|_{L_2} \lesssim_p \|V\|_{L_1} \le \|V\|_{L_q}. \] Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:master-diagonal-g} at \(q=2\) is comparable, up to constants depending only on \(p\), to its value at \(q\in[1,2)\), the lower bound extends to \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Extend via finite-chaos moment comparison.

nodes.name: Latala's moment estimate for i.i.d. centered sums
nodes.statement: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) be independent copies of a centered real-valued random variable \(Y\). Then, for every \(q\ge2\) such that \(Y\in L_q\), \begin{equation} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac qs \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nq\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|Y\|_{L_s}. \end{equation}
assumptions: \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) be independent copies of a centered real-valued random variable \(Y\)
conclusions: \begin{equation} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac qs \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nq\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|Y\|_{L_s}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided formula for the L_q norm of a sum of N i.i.d. centered variables as a supremum over s of (q/s)(N/q)^{1/s}||Y||_{L_s}.
nodes.label: lem:latala-iid-centered-sum

nodes.name: Latala two-sided estimate for centered i.i.d. sums (3.13)
nodes.statement: \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac qs \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac Nq\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \|Y\|_{L_s}.
nodes.label: eq:latala-iid-centered-sum

nodes.name: Weak moments of a single tensor power
nodes.statement: Let \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) be a centered sub-Gaussian random vector with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\), and let \(p\ge2\) be an integer. Then, for every \(q\ge1\), \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] Moreover, if \(X\) is Gaussian, then, for every \(q\ge1\), \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\| q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \] and \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]
assumptions: \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) be a centered sub-Gaussian random vector with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and sub-Gaussian constant \(K\)
conclusions: \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Directional moments of the centered tensor power: K^p(||Sigma||_F^{p/2} or odd-order analogue + ||Sigma||^{p/2}q^{p/2}); sharp two-sided Gaussian versions, centered and noncentered.
nodes.label: lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.3
nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, set \[ Z_i:=X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,N, \qquad Z:=X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}. \] We first consider \(q\ge2\). For \(\alpha\ge0\), define \[ \mathcal L_\alpha(N,q) := \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac qs \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac Nq \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} s^\alpha . \] An elementary optimization gives \begin{equation} \mathcal L_0(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{N(q\land N)}, \qquad \mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{Nq}, \end{equation} and, for every \(\alpha\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathcal L_\alpha(N,q) \asymp_\alpha \sqrt{Nq}+q^\alpha . \end{equation} We shall also use the fact that, for nonnegative \(f_s\) and \(g_s\), \begin{equation} \sup_s(f_s+g_s)\asymp\sup_s f_s+\sup_s g_s. \end{equation} \medskip \noindent\textbf{Sub-Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip Recall that \[ \rho_p(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] By Lemma~\ref{lem:latala-iid-centered-sum}, followed by interchanging the suprema over \(A\) and \(s\), we have \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac{q}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{N}{q}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle A,Z\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_s}. \end{align*} Applying the sub-Gaussian bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments} and \eqref{eq:sup-additivity}, we therefore obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_0(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_p(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} imply \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align} Indeed, the additional term \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\sqrt{Nq}\) arising from \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} is absorbed as follows. When \(p\) is even, it is absorbed by the first term if \(q\le N\), and by \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}\) if \(q>N\). When \(p\) is odd, it is absorbed by \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq}\). \medskip \noindent\textbf{Gaussian two-sided bound.} \medskip Suppose now that \(X\) is Gaussian. Repeating the preceding argument with the Gaussian two-sided estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments}, we obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_1(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} give \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align} It remains to consider \(1\le q<2\). The sub-Gaussian and Gaussian upper bounds follow from moment monotonicity and the corresponding estimates at \(q=2\), since their right-hand sides at \(q=2\) are bounded, up to constants depending only on \(p\), by those at \(q\). For the Gaussian lower bound, for every \(A\), the random variable \(\sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F}\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(p\) in Gaussian random variables. The finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} therefore gives \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_2} \lesssim_p \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_1} \le \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q}. \] Taking the supremum over \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), applying the Gaussian lower bound at \(q=2\), and comparing its right-hand side with that at \(q\) proves the desired lower bound for \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Latala's estimate (Lemma 3.4), interchange suprema, insert Lemma 3.5 and optimize the resulting Latala functionals; for q<2 use monotonicity and finite-chaos comparison.

nodes.name: Notation and elementary optimizations
nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, set \[ Z_i:=X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,N, \qquad Z:=X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}. \] We first consider \(q\ge2\). For \(\alpha\ge0\), define \[ \mathcal L_\alpha(N,q) := \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac qs \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \frac Nq \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} s^\alpha . \] An elementary optimization gives \begin{equation} \mathcal L_0(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{N(q\land N)}, \qquad \mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{Nq}, \end{equation} and, for every \(\alpha\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathcal L_\alpha(N,q) \asymp_\alpha \sqrt{Nq}+q^\alpha . \end{equation} We shall also use the fact that, for nonnegative \(f_s\) and \(g_s\), \begin{equation} \sup_s(f_s+g_s)\asymp\sup_s f_s+\sup_s g_s. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define Z_i, the Latala functional L_alpha and record its elementary asymptotics.

nodes.name: Elementary Latala optimization (3.14)
nodes.statement: \mathcal L_0(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{N(q\land N)}, \qquad \mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) \asymp \sqrt{Nq},
nodes.label: eq:elementary-latala-optimization

nodes.name: Elementary Latala optimization (power) (3.15)
nodes.statement: \mathcal L_\alpha(N,q) \asymp_\alpha \sqrt{Nq}+q^\alpha .
nodes.label: eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power

nodes.name: Additivity of suprema (3.16)
nodes.statement: \sup_s(f_s+g_s)\asymp\sup_s f_s+\sup_s g_s.
nodes.label: eq:sup-additivity

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip Recall that \[ \rho_p(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] By Lemma~\ref{lem:latala-iid-centered-sum}, followed by interchanging the suprema over \(A\) and \(s\), we have \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac{q}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{N}{q}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle A,Z\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_s}. \end{align*} Applying the sub-Gaussian bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments} and \eqref{eq:sup-additivity}, we therefore obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_0(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_p(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} imply \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align} Indeed, the additional term \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\sqrt{Nq}\) arising from \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} is absorbed as follows. When \(p\) is even, it is absorbed by the first term if \(q\le N\), and by \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}\) if \(q>N\). When \(p\) is odd, it is absorbed by \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq}\).
nodes.statement_short: Latala's estimate plus Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: Recall rho_p
nodes.statement: Recall that \[ \rho_p(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Recall the definition of rho_p.

nodes.name: Apply Latala's estimate
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:latala-iid-centered-sum}, followed by interchanging the suprema over \(A\) and \(s\), we have \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\asymp \sup_{\max\{2,q/N\}\le s\le q} \frac{q}{s} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{N}{q}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/s} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle A,Z\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_s}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.4 and interchange suprema.

nodes.name: Insert Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: Applying the sub-Gaussian bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments} and \eqref{eq:sup-additivity}, we therefore obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_0(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the single-tensor weak moment bound.

nodes.name: Optimize and absorb
nodes.statement: Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_p(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} imply \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align} Indeed, the additional term \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\sqrt{Nq}\) arising from \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} is absorbed as follows. When \(p\) is even, it is absorbed by the first term if \(q\le N\), and by \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}\) if \(q>N\). When \(p\) is odd, it is absorbed by \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq}\).
nodes.statement_short: Use (3.14)-(3.15) and absorb the extra term.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian scalar-sum bound (3.17)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p \begin{cases} \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{N(q\land N)} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:subgaussian-scalar-sum

nodes.name: Gaussian two-sided bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian two-sided bound.} \medskip Suppose now that \(X\) is Gaussian. Repeating the preceding argument with the Gaussian two-sided estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments}, we obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_1(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} give \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Repeat with the Gaussian two-sided estimate of Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: Gaussian Latala bound
nodes.statement: Suppose now that \(X\) is Gaussian. Repeating the preceding argument with the Gaussian two-sided estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:subgaussian-directional-tensor-moments}, we obtain \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_1(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathcal L_{1/2}(N,q) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\mathcal L_{p/2}(N,q), & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma) = \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided Latala estimate with the Gaussian bound of Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: Optimize
nodes.statement: Since \(\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\le\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\), \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization} and \eqref{eq:elementary-latala-optimization-power} give \begin{align} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Optimize the Latala functionals.

nodes.name: Gaussian scalar-sum two-sided bound (3.18)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \begin{cases} \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sqrt{Nq}+q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{Nq} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-scalar-sum

nodes.name: Upper bounds for q<2
nodes.statement: It remains to consider \(1\le q<2\). The sub-Gaussian and Gaussian upper bounds follow from moment monotonicity and the corresponding estimates at \(q=2\), since their right-hand sides at \(q=2\) are bounded, up to constants depending only on \(p\), by those at \(q\).
nodes.statement_short: Upper bounds for q<2 by monotonicity.

nodes.name: Gaussian lower bound for q<2
nodes.statement: For the Gaussian lower bound, for every \(A\), the random variable \(\sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F}\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(p\) in Gaussian random variables. The finite-chaos moment comparison \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} therefore gives \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_2} \lesssim_p \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_1} \le \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle A,Z_i\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg\|_{L_q}. \] Taking the supremum over \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), applying the Gaussian lower bound at \(q=2\), and comparing its right-hand side with that at \(q\) proves the desired lower bound for \(1\le q<2\). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Finite-chaos moment comparison extends the Gaussian lower bound.

nodes.name: Gaussian plus random-radius Rademacher example (sharpness and parity effect)
nodes.statement: Fix an integer \(p\ge2\). Let \[ \lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d>0, \qquad \Lambda:=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d), \qquad \lambda_1=\|\Lambda\|. \] Let \(G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Lambda)\), let \(\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^d\) have independent Rademacher entries, and let \(R\), independent of \(G\) and \(\varepsilon\), take the values \(0\) and \(\sqrt2\), each with probability \(1/2\). Define \[ Y:=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon, \qquad X:=(G,Y)\in\mathbb R^{2d}. \] Standard Gaussian and Rademacher sub-Gaussian estimates, together with the boundedness of \(R\), show that \(X\) satisfies \eqref{eq:def-subg} with \(K\asymp1\). Since \(\mathbb{E} R^2=1\), \(X\) is centered and has covariance matrix \[ \Sigma = \begin{bmatrix} \Lambda&0\\ 0&\Lambda \end{bmatrix}. \] Consequently, \begin{equation} \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)=2\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda), \qquad \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}=\sqrt2 \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}, \qquad \|\Sigma\|=\|\Lambda\|. \end{equation} For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), let \((G_i,R_i,\varepsilon_i)\) be independent copies of \((G,R,\varepsilon)\), and set \[ Y_i:=R_i\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon_i, \qquad X_i:=(G_i,Y_i). \] Then \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are i.i.d. with the same distribution as \(X\). Let \[ S_p := \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}. \] We show that, for every \(q\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \end{equation} where \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\) is defined in Theorem \ref{thm:main1}. Restricting \(S_p\) to the tensor block corresponding entirely to the \(G\)-coordinates, we obtain \[ \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The Gaussian lower bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} therefore yields \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation} Suppose first that \(p\) is odd. In this case, \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda) = \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Lambda\|^{1/2} = \rho_p(\Lambda). \] Moreover, $\sqrt{\frac qN} \ge \sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$. Thus \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} follows from \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}. Now suppose that \(p=2k\) is even. Retaining the first and third terms in \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower}, we have \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation} It remains to obtain the intermediate fluctuation scale lower bound. Set \[ B:=\frac{\Lambda}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}. \] Then \[ \|A\|_{\mathsf F} = \|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k = 1. \] Since $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}$ is the tensor block of \(S_p\) corresponding entirely to the \(Y\)-coordinates, we have \begin{equation} \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg| \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg|. \end{equation} Since \(Y=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon\) and every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) takes values in \(\{\pm 1\}\), \[ Y^\top B Y = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \varepsilon^\top\Lambda^2\varepsilon = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2 = R^2\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Consequently, recalling that \(p=2k\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},Y^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = (Y^\top B Y)^k = R^{2k}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k. \] For \( i = 1, \ldots, N\), define the Rademacher random variable \(\eta_i\) by \[ R_i^{2k}-\mathbb{E} R^{2k} = 2^{k-1}\eta_i. \] Then \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N\) are independent, and \[ \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} = 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i. \] Combining this identity with \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_block_test} and taking \(L_q\)-norms, we obtain \begin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \ge 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2} \sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}, \end{align} where the last step follows from the two-sided moment estimate for Rademacher sums \cite{montgomerysmith1990rademacher}. Combining \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_scales} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_middle_even}, and using \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}, proves \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} in the even case.
nodes.statement_short: X=(G,R Lambda^{1/2} eps) is sub-Gaussian with K~1 and attains all three terms of the sub-Gaussian bound; the Rademacher block produces the larger even-order scale rho_p.
nodes.label: example:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness

nodes.name: Covariance relations of the example (3.19)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)=2\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda), \qquad \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}=\sqrt2 \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}, \qquad \|\Sigma\|=\|\Lambda\|.
nodes.label: eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation

nodes.name: Lower bound attained by the example
nodes.statement: We show that, for every \(q\ge1\), \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \end{equation} where \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\) is defined in Theorem \ref{thm:main1}.
nodes.statement_short: For the example, the L_q Frobenius error is >~ Tr^{p/2}/sqrt(N) + rho_p sqrt((q^N)/N) + ||Sigma||^{p/2}q^{p/2}/N.
conclusions: \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}, \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lower bound to be shown in the example (3.20)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
nodes.label: eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness

nodes.name: Proof of the lower bound in Example 3.6
nodes.statement: Restricting \(S_p\) to the tensor block corresponding entirely to the \(G\)-coordinates, we obtain \[ \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The Gaussian lower bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} therefore yields \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation} Suppose first that \(p\) is odd. In this case, \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda) = \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Lambda\|^{1/2} = \rho_p(\Lambda). \] Moreover, $\sqrt{\frac qN} \ge \sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$. Thus \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} follows from \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}. Now suppose that \(p=2k\) is even. Retaining the first and third terms in \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower}, we have \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation} It remains to obtain the intermediate fluctuation scale lower bound. Set \[ B:=\frac{\Lambda}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}. \] Then \[ \|A\|_{\mathsf F} = \|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k = 1. \] Since $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}$ is the tensor block of \(S_p\) corresponding entirely to the \(Y\)-coordinates, we have \begin{equation} \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg| \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg|. \end{equation} Since \(Y=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon\) and every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) takes values in \(\{\pm 1\}\), \[ Y^\top B Y = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \varepsilon^\top\Lambda^2\varepsilon = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2 = R^2\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Consequently, recalling that \(p=2k\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},Y^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = (Y^\top B Y)^k = R^{2k}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k. \] For \( i = 1, \ldots, N\), define the Rademacher random variable \(\eta_i\) by \[ R_i^{2k}-\mathbb{E} R^{2k} = 2^{k-1}\eta_i. \] Then \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N\) are independent, and \[ \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} = 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i. \] Combining this identity with \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_block_test} and taking \(L_q\)-norms, we obtain \begin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \ge 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p Combining \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_scales} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_middle_even}, and using \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}, proves \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} in the even case.
nodes.statement_short: The Gaussian block plus the Gaussian lower bound of Theorem 2.1 gives the trace, large-deviation and odd intermediate scales; at even orders testing against (Lambda/||Lambda||_F)^{otimes k} reduces to a Rademacher sum.

nodes.name: Gaussian block lower bound
nodes.statement: Restricting \(S_p\) to the tensor block corresponding entirely to the \(G\)-coordinates, we obtain \[ \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The Gaussian lower bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:main1} therefore yields \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the Gaussian block and apply the Gaussian lower bound of Theorem 2.1.

nodes.name: Gaussian-block lower bound (3.21)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)\sqrt{\frac qN} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}.
nodes.label: eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower

nodes.name: Odd p
nodes.statement: Suppose first that \(p\) is odd. In this case, \[ \rho_{p,G}(\Lambda) = \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Lambda\|^{1/2} = \rho_p(\Lambda). \] Moreover, $\sqrt{\frac qN} \ge \sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$. Thus \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} follows from \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}.
nodes.statement_short: At odd p the Gaussian intermediate scale already equals rho_p.

nodes.name: Even p
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \(p=2k\) is even. Retaining the first and third terms in \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower}, we have \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation} It remains to obtain the intermediate fluctuation scale lower bound. Set \[ B:=\frac{\Lambda}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}. \] Then \[ \|A\|_{\mathsf F} = \|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k = 1. \] Since $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}$ is the tensor block of \(S_p\) corresponding entirely to the \(Y\)-coordinates, we have \begin{equation} \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg| \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg|. \end{equation} Since \(Y=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon\) and every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) takes values in \(\{\pm 1\}\), \[ Y^\top B Y = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \varepsilon^\top\Lambda^2\varepsilon = \frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}} \sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2 = R^2\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Consequently, recalling that \(p=2k\), \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},Y^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = (Y^\top B Y)^k = R^{2k}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k. \] For \( i = 1, \ldots, N\), define the Rademacher random variable \(\eta_i\) by \[ R_i^{2k}-\mathbb{E} R^{2k} = 2^{k-1}\eta_i. \] Then \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N\) are independent, and \[ \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} = 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i. \] Combining this identity with \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_block_test} and taking \(L_q\)-norms, we obtain \begin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \ge 2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i \bigg\|_{L_q} \asymp_p \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2} \sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}, \end{align} where the last step follows from the two-sided moment estimate for Rademacher sums \cite{montgomerysmith1990rademacher}. Combining \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_scales} and \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_middle_even}, and using \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_covariance_relation}, proves \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_sharpness} in the even case.
nodes.statement_short: At even p the Rademacher block yields the larger intermediate scale.

nodes.name: Trace and large-deviation scales
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \(p=2k\) is even. Retaining the first and third terms in \eqref{eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_lower}, we have \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Keep the first and third terms of (3.21).

nodes.name: Trace and large-deviation scales (3.22)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \gtrsim_p \frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N} + \|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}.
nodes.label: eq:subgaussian_tensor_gaussian_scales

nodes.name: Test tensor
nodes.statement: It remains to obtain the intermediate fluctuation scale lower bound. Set \[ B:=\frac{\Lambda}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}. \] Then \[ \|A\|_{\mathsf F} = \|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k = 1. \]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce B=Lambda/||Lambda||_F and A=B^{otimes k}.

nodes.name: Block test
nodes.statement: Since $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}$ is the tensor block of \(S_p\) corresponding entirely to the \(Y\)-coordinates, we have \begin{equation} \|S_p\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg\| \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\|_{\mathsf F} \ge \bigg| \bigg\langle A, \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p} \bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F} \bigg|. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the Y-block and test against A.

nodes.name: Rademacher-block test (3.23)
